steps.title: The three-variable relationship
steps.content: Distance, speed and time are linked: distance = speed × time. Rearrange to find speed or time. Keep units consistent before calculating.
steps.formula:
Distance = Speed × Time
Speed = Distance ÷ Time
Time = Distance ÷ Speed
steps.example: A car travels at 60 km/h for 2.5 hours. Distance = 60×2.5 = 150 km.

steps.title: Find the distance
steps.prompt: A bus travels at 45 km/h for 4 hours. How far does it travel?

steps.title: Convert units
steps.content: To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5. Convert minutes to hours when speed is in km/h.

steps.title: Convert speed
steps.prompt: Convert 54 km/h into metres per second.

steps.title: Relative speed
steps.content: When two objects move in opposite directions, relative speed is the sum of their speeds. When they move in the same direction, relative speed is the difference.
steps.example: Two trains at 50 and 40 km/h in opposite directions approach each other at 90 km/h.
